column2: NOT PORTED, AND IT IS THEIR DEFAULT
column3: cuML olsFit defaults to algo=0, one-sided Jacobi SVD. Normal equations SQUARE the condition number, so lstsqEig loses about twice the digits on an ill-conditioned design. sklearn's LinearRegression uses LAPACK gelsd, also an SVD route, so this difference belongs in any accuracy comparison

column2: NOT PORTED; ridgeEig (algo 1, cuML's Python 'eig'/'auto') IS (DEVIATION 545)
column3: The sentence that stood here -- "ridge is lstsqEig with alpha added to the eigenvalues before inverting. Cheap once wanted" -- was WRONG about their design: ridgeEig is svdEig (an SVD via the Gram's eigendecomposition, U = A V / S) followed by ridgeSolve's six RAFT ops with two ABSOLUTE thresholds on a singular value; see glm/impl/glm/ridge.mojo. ridgeSVD needs cuSOLVER gesvd (svdQR), no equivalent; n_cols == 1 forces it (ridge.cuh:210) and is refused by name. ridgeSolve's thres=1e-10 and svdEig's 1e-10 are absolute, the OLS_NONZERO_THRESH deviation again, carried and gated (ridge.solve.nnz is the card's integer stage)

column2: PORTED 2026-08-23 as glm/impl/glm/preprocess.mojo (unweighted arms, by the cd lane; moved here from solver/), but ols_fit does NOT call it; the DEVICE preprocess is unreached. NOT a user-facing gap: fit_intercept=True is honored, by centering X and y on the HOST in float64 and forming the intercept with math.fsum (DEVIATION 517, python/mojolearn/linear_model.py:46-56). MEASURED 2026-09-01: a planted model with intercept 7.25 comes back coef [1.5 -2.0 0.5 3.0] intercept 7.25000 exactly. What is owed is moving that centering onto the device, not the feature
column3: LinearRegression(fit_intercept=True) is cuML's PYTHON DEFAULT (linear_regression.pyx:309), so their default fit is preProcessData -> lstsqEig -> postProcessData, not lstsqEig alone. preProcessData centers X by column means and y by its mean (preprocess.cuh:98,100,115,117); postProcessData sets intercept = mean(y) - mu_X . coef and UNDOES both centerings in place (preprocess.cuh:148-176). ols_fit refuses fit_intercept and defaults it False, i.e. it mirrors the fit_intercept=False branch, which on their side also sets *intercept = 0 (ols.cuh:156). core/column_stats.mojo already has the kernels. normalize is only reachable with fit_intercept and is the meanvar/colNorm arm at preprocess.cuh:76-108

column2: PORTED WITH AN ABSOLUTE THRESHOLD, RECORDED AS A DEVIATION
column3: `OLS_NONZERO_THRESH` is 1.0e-10 and is compared against an eigenvalue of A^T A, a quantity that scales with the SQUARE of the data and with n_rows. MEASURED (check_ols_rank_guard_is_absolute): the same 4096x8 design has rank 8 at scale 1 and rank 0 at scale 2^-24, i.e. the same design in different units returns the zero model. Same defect class as jacobi_eigh_device.mojo DEVIATION BLOCK 1, which was fixed by making the test relative. NOT fixed here because glm/ported is COPY-DO-NOT-IMPROVE and the change moves shipped NUMERIC_FAST bits near the boundary. Identity consequence: the comparison's output is a RANK, so at the boundary a per-vendor last bit changes how many directions the model has, not its fifth decimal
